definition: RiTa is an open-source software toolkit for generative writing and English natural language, originally developed using the Java language by Daniel C.
details: Howe and collaborators, and later implemented in JavaScript as rita.js. Current versions of RiTa (Version 3.0 was released in 2023) are implemented in both Java and JavaScript and integrate with p5.js, Processing, Node and Android.

explainer.lead: RiTa is an open-source software toolkit for generative writing and English natural language, originally developed in Java by Daniel C. Howe and collaborators and later implemented in JavaScript as rita.js. It matters because it gives writers and developers a ready-made toolkit for generative text work.

tiers.eli5: It is a free box of tools that helps a program write and play with English words.
tiers.practitioner: Current versions are implemented in both Java and JavaScript, so engineers integrate RiTa with p5.js, Processing, Node, and Android. A pitfall to remember is that it targets English natural language specifically.
tiers.paperLevel: RiTa is an open-source toolkit for generative writing and English natural language; Version 3.0 was released in 2023, and current versions are implemented in both Java and JavaScript.

explainer.example: A developer building a sketch in p5.js can use rita.js for generative writing within the same environment.
